title: FIG. 05 · Phase ledger
summary: The method set as one working instrument: the same head as the rest of the page, then a panel that lists the four phases on the left (what each one delivers, and who runs it) and draws them as a schedule on the right, row for row. The red ten-day audit comes first, then a Handover line, then your Calibrate line runs out of the panel and off the page.
story: The section above shows what you keep when we leave; this one shows how you get there, starting with the small, fixed audit, and makes 'revenue architecture as a service' concrete: we diagnose, design and install, hand over, and then it keeps running under your operator or with us on retainer. It hands 'the audit' straight to the next section, which opens with 'The audit is a gate'.
motion: Head (standalone and live): the label fades in, 'It starts with' and the lighter 'the audit.' rise out of their masks, the short red rule draws, and the lede and the Engagements note fade up. This is the same entrance as every other section head.

Instrument: the panel rises in. The scale along its top calibrates: its line draws across the full width while the day ticks arrive left to right, slightly off-pitch, and settle into place. The seam between the list and the schedule draws down.

Then the phases build in reading order, about 0.6 seconds apart. Each row's name, output and 'run by' rise in, then its bar extends. Diagnose goes first, in red, and the ten day ticks above it light up one by one as the bar passes beneath them, so the scale visibly measures the audit; its '10 working days · the System Audit' label then appears. Architect and Install follow. The Handover line draws down through the panel and out of both its edges, with its label. Calibrate's row rises, its bar runs from the Handover line out of the panel and off the page, and 'Yours' appears. Everything has landed by about 4.8 seconds.

Ambient (the page's only loop besides the hero film): a small dark square rides the Calibrate bar from the Handover line off the page, one lap every 9.6 seconds, steady and slow. It pauses whenever the section is off screen.

On the live page: the head plays as the section arrives, but the panel holds its first frame until it is about a third in view, so the build happens where you can see it. It plays once and does not replay when you scroll back. Hovering a row lights it and its bar.
Reduced motion: the finished panel appears at once, with every bar drawn and no moving square.
addressed: Your note: 'it seems a little too empty.' The section is now one dense, readable instrument with no empty corners. The four phases sit in a ledger (number, phase, what you get, who runs it), and each phase's bar sits in the same row beside it. The empty diagonal and the big blank areas from round 3 are gone.

Your note: 'an abrupt change in design language compared to other sections.' It speaks the page's language again: the same label, two-line statement, red rule and lede as the reframe and the handover, a quiet note at the top right like round 2's method, one flat panel, a calibrated scale and a small title block. It deliberately does not reuse the reframe's caption strip and toggle, so the layout still varies down the page.

You approved round 2's phase chart, so the chart stays, now as the right half of the instrument and lined up with the phases it measures. You can read across any row: Diagnose, what it delivers, Kelwin runs it, ten working days.

'Revenue architecture as a service' is made concrete in one glance. The 'Run by' column reads Kelwin, Kelwin, Kelwin, then 'Your operator, or us on retainer'. On the schedule, Kelwin's dashed lanes stop at the Handover line, and only Calibrate keeps running, out of the panel and off the page, labelled Yours. The note above says the model in your own words: install first, then an operating retainer, on a system you own.

The audit is the one lit step, as agreed: the only red bar, the only measured span on the scale (ten lit day ticks), and the only duration printed. Everything else is marked Indicative, so no timelines are invented.

(round 2's approved wording), the Run-by cell reads 'Your operator, or us on retainer', and the bar carries 'Yours'.
